sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 14.7% a year from $96.6 billion in FY2017 to $331.8 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F221].
Operating income grew faster, at 20.5% a year, lifting operating margin from 30.1% to 46.8% [F223][F41][F50].
FY2026 was the sharpest step, with revenue up 17.8% on growth in Microsoft Cloud, Azure and Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud [D472][P17].
FY2018 broke the net-income line, falling 35.0% on the TCJA charge, while FY2019 rebounded 136.8% on a $2.6 billion intangible-property tax benefit [D48][D101][P61].
Microsoft Cloud supplied 16.2pp of FY2026's 17.8% revenue growth and reached 64.6% of revenue [D568][D472][D566].
Server products and cloud services added 11.0pp, as Azure and other cloud services grew 41% on demand across workloads [D642][P12].
Microsoft 365 Commercial products and cloud services contributed 5.1pp, with cloud revenue up 17% on Copilot and E5 [D649][P14].
Profit outran revenue: incremental operating margin was 53.3% in FY2026 and operating expenses grew 7.4% against 17.8% revenue growth [D498][D491][D472].
Diluted EPS grew 31.6% against 31.3% net income growth, with the diluted share count down 0.2% [D476][D474][D493].
Operating margin of 46.8% is a window high, 5.1pp above the 41.7% median and 16.7pp above the FY2017 low [F50][D974][D975][D973].
Gross margin slipped 0.9pp to 67.9%, below its 68.2% median, as cost of revenue grew 21.1% against 17.8% revenue growth [D486][F30][D981][D489][D472].

The FY2026 operating-margin gain came from R&D (+0.8pp) and other lines (+1.2pp), partly offset by cost of revenue (-0.9pp), with operating expenses up 7% on R&D compute, AI talent and XBOX impairment [D501][D502][D500][P16].
Intelligent Cloud gross margin fell on continued AI infrastructure investment and mix shift to Azure, partly offset by Azure efficiency gains [P11].
Net margin rose 4.2pp to 40.3%, helped by $6.5 billion of net OpenAI gains in other income [D488][F70][P7].
Operating cash flow of $182.9 billion was 1.37x net income, but free cash flow of $67.0 billion was only 0.50x, the window low [F100][D459][F120][D460][D988].
Capex rose 79.6% to $115.9 billion, 34.9% of revenue, as additions to property and equipment increased $51.4 billion [D479][F110][D455][P1].
Free cash flow margin fell to 20.2% from a 30.3% median, and capex ran at 3.38x D&A [D456][D984][D461].
Operating cash flow growth of 34.4% came from higher customer receipts and lower income-tax payments, partly offset by supplier payments [D477][P1].
Net cash was $72.9 billion, 22.0% of revenue, in the 83rd percentile of six software peers against a -7.2% median [D465][D466][D1006][D1007].
Total debt fell to $40.3 billion while cash and investments held at $113.2 billion, and the current ratio of 1.23x is a window low [D464][D463][F200][D991].
Buybacks of $22.3 billion plus dividends of $26.4 billion absorbed 72.7% of free cash flow [X147][X157][D468].
The diluted share count fell only 0.2%, so per-share growth came from earnings rather than shrinkage [D493].
Free cash flow stayed below 80% of net income for two years, at 0.70x in FY2025 and 0.50x in FY2026, the lowest in the window [R1][D406][D460][D988].
The gap is capex-led, with FY2026 additions to property and equipment up $51.4 billion and other investing up $22.2 billion for components [P1].
FY2017 pretax income, tax and receivables were later restated, so FY2017 ratios such as the 8.4% tax rate rest on first-reported values [R2][R3][R4][D10].
Product revenue members overlap, summing to 180% of FY2026 consolidated revenue, so they should not be added [R5].
If capex as a share of revenue stays above the FY2026 34.9%, free cash flow margin will likely remain under the 20.2% window low [D455][D456][D982].
Watch operating margin against the 46.8% high; a drop toward the 41.7% median would reverse the leverage trend [F50][D975].
Watch Microsoft Cloud's 64.6% revenue share and 26.9% growth; a slowdown below the FY2025 22.7% would mark a new phase [D566][D567][D564].
